title: Introduce timebound operator delegations, audit-normalizer middleware, and tenant-scoped KMS proxy
author: Nina Chen
description:
Motivation: operators that perform cross-tenant actions (support tooling, operator-runbooks, and emergency remediation agents) currently rely on long-lived delegated credentials which complicate audit trails and increase blast radius. This PR introduces three coordinated changes: 1) RBAC v2 timebound delegations (operator_delegation scope + ttl and attenuation rules), 2) an audit-normalizer middleware that canonicalizes operator identities, strips sensitive payload fragments and emits deterministic audit fingerprints, and 3) a tenant-scoped KMS proxy that wraps delegated keys with per-tenant envelopes and supports automated key rotation without changing delegation metadata.

Summary of changes: implemented a new operator delegation model (service/authz/delegation.go and api/rbac/policy_v2.yaml) that supports scoped TTLs, attenuation rules and delegation-chaining limits; added audit normalizer (service/audit/normalizer.go) which canonicalizes agent IDs, scrubs potentially sensitive fields from request payloads based on data-class labels, and emits a compact audit fingerprint used by downstream dedupe/retention jobs; introduced tenant-scoped KMS proxy (service/kms/proxy.go) which wraps delegated symmetric keys with tenant CMK envelopes and exposes a lightweight rotate endpoint (internal only) to perform non-disruptive wrapping rotations.

Why this is different: previous changes focused on region/KMS residency and per-request assertions. This PR emphasizes minimizing operator blast radius and improving audit signal quality (canonicalization + deterministic fingerprints) while enabling safe key rotation for delegated artifacts. The audit-normalizer is intentionally configurable per-tenant policy to respect sovereignty and PII constraints.

Checklist: 
- [x] RBAC schema additions and enforcement middleware
- [x] Audit normalizer implementation + unit tests
- [x] Tenant KMS proxy + integration tests against KMS emulator
- [x] Backwards-compatible migration path and feature flag
- [x] Docs: developer guide and security playbook
- [x] Observability: metrics + alerts for delegation mismatches

Migration notes: the new RBAC v2 fields (delegation_ttl_seconds, attenuation_profile) are optional. Existing long-lived delegations are accepted but will be marked with a compatibility flag and subject to a rolling attenuation enforcement window (30 days) via feature-flagged rollout. Tenant administrators can opt into audit-normalizer policies and KMS proxy by setting tenant.features.operator_delegation = true.

Security review: SEC-147 notes included; audit-normalizer has explicit allowlist for fields to scrub and a configurable redaction level per tenant. KMS proxy interacts only with tenant CMKs and logs only envelope metadata (no raw key material).

References: Linear ENG-3219 (operator delegation overhaul), security note SEC-147, internal runbook: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3219, design doc: /docs/design/operator-delegations.md

Release notes: Adds timebound operator delegations (RBAC v2), a configurable audit normalizer middleware to improve audit signal and privacy, and a tenant-scoped KMS proxy to support non-disruptive key rotation for delegated artifacts. Admins must review tenant feature flags and optionally opt into the new behavior.

notes_for_ops: Feature rollout is behind featureflag operator_delegation_v2. Rollout plan: gradual enable per-tenant over 4 weeks; watch metrics 'delegation_mismatch' and 'audit_normalizer_redactions'. If high match-failure rates occur, rollback via feature flag for affected tenant.
